Magnet A is slowly moved towards magnet B. This causes magnet B to move away from magnet A.

On Fig. 1.1, label the magnetic poles and sketch the magnetic field around the two magnets.
parts.solution_md:
The magnetic field lines are drawn as follows:

Between two S poles:

![20-1-m-ma1a-2-sq-cie-ial-physics](assets/002-20-1-m-ma1a-2-sq-cie-ial-physics.png)

Between two N poles:

![20-1-m-ma1a-1-sq-cie-ial-physics](assets/003-20-1-m-ma1a-1-sq-cie-ial-physics.png)

- Magnetic field lines between two like poles (both S poles **OR** both N poles) showing repulsion; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Two bar magnets, A and B, are placed next to each other as shown in Fig. 1.1. Magnet A is slowly moved towards magnet B. This causes magnet B to move away from magnet A.

Magnet A is swapped for a magnet which is twice as strong but keeps the same orientation.

Describe how the magnetic field around magnet B would change.
parts.solution_md:
If the strength of magnet A was doubled:

- There would be twice as many field lines; **[1 mark]**
- The field lines would be closer together at the poles; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
Fig. 1.1 shows a magnet held close to a second magnet which is suspended by a light cotton thread.

![fig-1-7-1-medium-aqa-gcse-physics](assets/005-fig-1-7-1-medium-aqa-gcse-physics.png)

**Fig. 1.1**

Describe how a magnetic field is produced around a bar magnet.
parts.solution_md:
A magnetic field is produced around a bar magnet by:

- The movement of electrons within the atoms of the magnet; **[1 mark]**
- Electrons circulate around atoms, acting like a small current, and set up a magnetic field; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
State and explain whether

(i) a stationary charge will produce a magnetic field

[2]

(ii) a current-carrying wire will produce a magnetic field.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
(i) A stationary charge:

- Will <u>not</u> produce a magnetic field; **[1 mark]**
- Because the charge must be moving (to produce a magnetic field); **[1 mark]**

(ii) A current-carrying wire:

- Will produce a magnetic field; **[1 mark]**
- Because current is the movement of charge / electrons; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**
